newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER WEDNESDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE TO FIRMER WEDNESDAY.

text.p: HARARE, June 18 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable to firmer on Wednesday, dealers said.
The market opened with a Z$26.6 million surplus and liquidity was boosted with the maturity of around Z$600 million worth of treasury bills.
The central Reserve Bank auctioned 91-day treasury bills amounting to Z$600 million with an average yield of 24.99 percent, a notch up from 24.98 percent at Tuesday's sale.
Treasury bills were changing hands on the secondary market at 24.55, up from Tuesday's 24.25 percent but call money was quoted unchanged at 22 percent.
NCD bills with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26 from 25 26 percent but sold at a stable 25 percent.
Bank acceptance bills were quoted 25.5 from 25 percent (buying) and but were stable at 24.5 percent on the sell-side.
